hypotheses.text: Early-onset nystagmus (HP:0000639) and hypotonia (HP:0001252) progressing to spastic quadriparesis (HP:0001257) are present in >85% of infantile-onset NKX6-2 cases, whereas secondary features such as seizures (HP:0001250) and developmental regression (HP:0002376) occur in fewer than 35% of the global pooled cohort.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying exact pooled phenotypic penetrance distinguishes invariant core manifestations from lower-frequency findings that complicate differential diagnosis from epileptic or metabolic encephalopathies.

evidence.text: Baldi et al. identified 10 new patients from 6 unrelated families where all shared psychomotor delay, spastic quadriparesis, nystagmus, and hypotonia, whereas seizures were restricted to 2 families and developmental regression to 3 families.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and genetic spectra of NKX6‐2‐related disorder
source.quote: Our patients share a primary diagnosis of psychomotor delay, and they show spastic quadriparesis, nystagmus and hypotonia. Seizures and dysmorphic features (observed in 2 families each) represent an addition to the phenotype, while developmental regression (observed in 3 families) appears to be a notable and previously underestimated clinical feature.

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2020) combined previously reported cases with 11 newly identified cases across 8 families and observed that phenotypic expression encompasses epilepsy occurring without overt hypomyelination as well as diffuse hypomyelination without seizures.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: Eleven new cases from eight families of different ethnic backgrounds carrying compound heterozygous and homozygous pathogenic variants in NKX6-2 were identified... it is shown that phenotypes with epilepsy in the absence of overt hypomyelination and diffuse hypomyelination without seizures can occur.

hypotheses.text: Cerebral hypomyelination (HP:0003429) is absent on neuroimaging in approximately 20% to 30% of published biallelic NKX6-2 individuals, who present instead with childhood-onset spastic ataxia and isolated cerebellar atrophy (HP:0001272).
hypotheses.rationale: Differential diagnosis algorithms frequently exclude SPAX8 when diffuse hypomyelination is absent; establishing the exact frequency of hypomyelination-negative cohorts will prevent underdiagnosis of NKX6-2 spastic ataxia.

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2017) demonstrated that in 7 individuals from 3 families, affected members from 2 families exhibited childhood-onset disease with slow progression and predominant cerebellar atrophy rather than overt brain hypomyelination, while hypomyelination was restricted to the third family.

source.title: Mutations in NKX6-2 cause progressive spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: We report seven individuals with an early-onset spastic-ataxia phenotype. The individuals come from three families of different ethnic backgrounds. Affected members of two families had childhood onset disease with very slow progression. They are still alive in their 30s and 40s and show predominant ataxia and cerebellar atrophy features on imaging. Affected members of the third family had a similar but earlier-onset presentation associated with brain hypomyelination.

numbers.metric: families with childhood onset and cerebellar atrophy without predominant hypomyelination

hypotheses.text: Clinically evident peripheral axonal neuropathy (HP:0003477) with distal extremity drop is an atypical manifestation present in under 10% of all published NKX6-2 cases.
hypotheses.rationale: If peripheral neuropathy is documented in only isolated kindreds, its presence is not required for diagnosis and its absence cannot rule out SPAX8.

evidence.text: Bereshneh et al. (2020) reported wrist drop and foot drop due to peripheral axonal neuropathy in 2 affected siblings carrying the homozygous c.501C>G p.(Phe167Leu) variant, explicitly identifying peripheral axonal neuropathy as a novel clinical expansion.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and neuroimaging features of NKX6 ...
source.quote: two affected siblings with main manifestations of global developmental delay, motor regression, hypotonia, clonus in lower limbs and muscle bulk atrophy especially in the upper limbs, spasticity and contracture, scoliosis, hip dislocation, oculomotor apraxia, horizontal and vertical nystagmus. In addition, wrist and foot drop due to peripheral axonal neuropathy were observed in these patients as a new clinical finding

numbers.metric: affected siblings with peripheral axonal neuropathy

new_directions.question_text: What is the pooled worldwide frequency of developmental regression (HP:0002376) in NKX6-2 patients, and is regression provoked by intercurrent infections or metabolic triggers?
new_directions.rationale: Baldi et al. (2018) highlighted developmental regression in 3 out of 6 families as an underestimated finding. Determining its triggers and true pooled prevalence will resolve whether SPAX8 can mimic neurodegenerative or episodic neurometabolic conditions.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of published NKX6-2 patients develop secondary musculoskeletal complications (scoliosis HP:0002650, hip dislocation HP:0002827, and limb contractures HP:0001371) by age group?
new_directions.rationale: Bereshneh et al. reported contractures, scoliosis, and hip dislocation. Establishing the penetrance of orthopedic deformities will clarify the secondary burden of long-standing spasticity across pediatric and adult cohorts.
